summary: Fade's two-stop linear ramp is replaced by a perceptual one (new lib item fade-ramp): a Gaussian penumbra sampled at seventeen stops, so there is no corner at either end to read as a stripe or a start line, plus a dark-scheme table that leaves the same perceptual fraction of ink visible as light does (light ink under a dark veil kept 53% of its lightness at 0.5 alpha against 46% in light, so dark trails lingered). Depths move one step to 24/48/96 (sm/md/lg) because the eased ramp's first quarter is under 9% alpha — md 48 covers about what linear 32 did, and dissolves where that one ghosted a single line. fadeMask uses the same profile as the paint's complement. Chosen by rendering six curves at four depths over the shipped copy in both schemes (fade.doc.ts, knownGaps 'Ramp research').

migration.manual: Callers that sized a layout around the band's depth (an action slot placed relative to a 32px ramp, a sticky region offset by -32px) re-check against 48px for md, 24px for sm and 96px for lg. To keep an old depth, set --ui-fade-band-depth on the band's style.
